name: L'Amour
remarks: Year and perfumer from retailer and database pages, no brand page read. One retailer puts orange blossom at the top instead of neroli. White floral with a musky woody base.

name: Chamade pour Homme
remarks: Pyramid quoted from Guerlain's own description on the review page. Conceived as a male answer to the 1969 Chamade. Sold as discontinued by decant retailers. 'Woods' stands for 'precious wood'.

name: Guess 1981 for Men
remarks: Retailer pyramid, consistent across several listings. 'Incense' stands for olibanum. Not to be confused with the 2019 flanker Guess 1981 Los Angeles. Perfumer not found in allowed sources.

name: L'Eau Bleue
remarks: Launch: Harrods exclusive from 1 February 2017, nationwide from 29 March 2017 (UK press). Press notes: lily of the valley, dew, honeysuckle, akigalawood. Nordstrom lists wild rose in the heart. 'Watery Notes' stands for the dew accord. Musk appears on some retailer pages only. Flanker of Miu Miu (2015).

name: Encre Noire à l'Extrême
remarks: Launched October 2015 in France (Auparfum), Harrods exclusive in the UK before a wider 2016 rollout. Made for the tenth anniversary of Encre Noire (2006), same perfumer. Auparfum's press list differs slightly (grapefruit, lavandin, nutmeg, cashmere wood).

name: Musc Élixir Précieux
remarks: Perfume oil from Les Élixirs Précieux (2014, with Ambre, Oud, Rose), meant for layering with La Collection Privée. No published note pyramid found. Reported discontinued by 2023. Skip.

name: Aqua Kenzo pour Femme
remarks: Flat list on the page read; tier split matches several retailer listings seen in search. Some retailers credit Louise Turner but this was not confirmed on a page read, so perfumer left null.

name: Dolce Rosa Excelsa
remarks: Flanker of Dolce (2014). Year 2016 per Le Parfumier and others, some US retailers say 2014. Rose is listed as damask and Turkish rose. Nordstrom marks it sold out.

name: L'Eau de Paille
remarks: Launched February 2016, fourth in the L'Eau series after L'Eau Serge Lutens, L'Eau Froide and Laine de Verre. Official notes: vetiver, incense, grains. Hay and green notes reflect the straw theme; tonka is what the NST reviewer smelled. Perfumer often given as Christopher Sheldrake but not confirmed on a page read.

name: Pasha Édition Noire Sport
remarks: Flanker of Pasha Édition Noire (2013). Nordstrom: honeydew, fougère heart with citrus, cedar. Other retailers: citrus and watery top, sea notes, cedar, sandalwood, amber base. Pyramid merged. Mathilde Laurent only suggested by a blogger, perfumer left null.

name: Infusion de Mimosa
remarks: Part of Les Infusions de Prada, 2016. Official base is only 'a subtle woodiness'. Some US retailers list a different pyramid for a later 'Les Infusions Mimosa' bottle.

name: Amor Amor in a Flash
remarks: Limited edition flanker of Amor Amor (2003), from April 2013. Osmoz lists tangerine, apricot / apple, toffee / vanilla, cinnamon and labels it EDP; most retailers sell it as EDT and add jasmine, sandalwood, caramel. Pyramid merged.

name: Les Gourmandises de Luna
remarks: Limited edition of Luna, summer 2017, sprinkle-decorated bottle. Notes: pear granita, pink grapefruit cream, coconut milk, white peony, Sri Lankan sandalwood, caramel.

name: Modern Princess Eau Sensuelle
remarks: Flanker of Modern Princess (2016). Grapefruit is pink grapefruit. One retailer credits Christophe Raynaud, not confirmed on a page read.

name: Cologne Take Me Out
remarks: Part of the 2019 Mugler Cologne line (on sale 29 April 2019 per Auparfum; retailers say 2018). Only orange blossom, shiso leaf and a secret 'P' molecule are published; retailer pyramids conflict. Skip.

name: 1881 Riviera
remarks: Men's flanker of Cerruti 1881 pour Homme, inspired by Saint-Tropez. Several retailers credit Michel Girard, not confirmed on a page read.

name: Sì Passione Red Maestro
remarks: Limited edition flanker of Sì Passione (2017), red lacquered bottle with ribbon. Official heart is a 'solar jasmine accord'. Year 2019 per retailers; listed as discontinued by Wikiparfum (search result).

name: Aqua Universalis
remarks: Brand lists Sicilian lemon, Calabrian bergamot, lily of the valley, sweet mock orange (seringa), light musky woods. Aldehydes placed in the heart from Luckyscent's main notes. Also exists as candle and laundry products.

name: Knowing
remarks: Firmenich creation by Elie Roger (Bois de Jasmin, Now Smell This); some retailers wrongly credit Jean Kerléo. Flat note list split into tiers. Rose chypre; modern versions lean more on patchouli than oakmoss.

name: Boucheron Fleurs
remarks: Flanker of Boucheron (1988), presented as a more transparent take on the original floriental. Petalia is a Firmenich captive. Some retailers list mandarin and lemon in place of citron.
